sections.title: Fronds and growth
sections.text: Pteridium aquilinum, bracken, is a rhizomatous fern that forms large triangular fronds, often about 1 m tall or more. New fronds emerge as coiled fiddleheads; sori run along the underside of the leaf margins.

sections.title: Toxicity and food
sections.text: Young fronds and rhizomes have been eaten traditionally, but bracken contains toxic and carcinogenic compounds and is associated with serious health risks. It should not be treated as a safe food; the available sources do not guarantee safety after processing.
